name: King of the sons of Ammon
overview: The King of the sons of Ammon was a male ruler reigning during the time of King Zedekiah of Judah, as noted in Jeremiah 27:3. His tribal affiliation is not specified, and there are no additional personal notes recorded about him. He is identified primarily by his position as king over the Ammonites during this significant historical period.
namesAndTitles: This figure is known by the title 'King of the sons of Ammon,' which literally means 'king of the sons of Ammon' in Hebrew. This title is descriptive rather than a personal name and was not given by God. It emphasizes his role as the sovereign leader of the Ammonite people.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for this person beyond his role as king during Zedekiah's reign. There are no known familial ties or relationships documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: The King of the sons of Ammon is significant as a contemporary ruler during the reign of Judah's last king, Zedekiah, situating him within the broader geopolitical context of Jeremiah's prophetic ministry. His mention highlights the interactions and political dynamics between Judah and neighboring nations during a critical time preceding the Babylonian exile. Although details about his actions are sparse, his presence in the narrative underscores the regional alliances and tensions of the period.
